subject: POC trial environment setup - hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (post-call recap)
messages:

Subject: POC trial environment setup - hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (post-call recap)

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps to get the POC (trial) moving:

Summary of requirements (from conversation)
- Primary goal: validate latency and cost-per-token for FinLytics' extraction pipeline (batch job + interactive Q&A).
- Success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 350ms for interactive flows; batch throughput >= 4000 tokens/sec for nightly ETL; end-to-end cost target <$0.004/token across typical workload mix.
- Data constraints: PII must remain in your VPC for regulated customers; initial run will use de-identified data.

POC options we discussed (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted environment using our shared hosted API + customer-specific workspace. Pros: fastest to start; no infra setup. Cons: not suitable if you need VPC isolation for PII.
2) Dedicated sandbox: reserved GPU pool in our Dedicated offering (isolated but managed by Redwood). Pros: predictable throughput and realistic perf. Cons: takes ~2 business days to provision.
3) VPC trial (customer-managed infra): Redwood Private (VPC peering or customer-hosted). Pros: full network isolation, aligns with your security. Cons: longer setup (1-2 weeks) depending on networking / KMS.

Recommended path for this POC based on timeline and security: start with a quick hosted trial to validate model selection and baseline cost/latency (3-5 days), then migrate the most promising config to a Dedicated sandbox for realistic throughput testing. If you need VPC for compliance we'll run a parallel VPC trial in the second week.

Ownership & timeline
- Redwood owner: Marissa (me) — project lead, setup + onboarding.
- FinLytics owner: Sara Kim — technical lead; Tom for procurement/security.
- Proposed timeline: Hosted start: Wed Mar 3 (3-5 days), Dedicated sandbox: provision by Mon Mar 8, VPC kickoff: Mar 10 if needed.

Next steps
1) Sara: confirm which dataset (de-identified or sample) you want us to ingest for the hosted run.
2) Tom / Procurement: confirm any procurement timelines for Dedicated / Private.
3) We'll share a short POC mattersheet and VPC checklist (attached) and a short eval plan with test prompts and metrics.

Attachments: poc-mattersheet.pdf (application/pdf), vpc-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min sync if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the notes. A couple of operational items we should lock before hosted start:
- Rate limits: for the hosted trial we should pre-configure a per-minute quota for FinLytics to avoid noisy neighbors impacting latency. Suggest 120 reqs/min to start.
- Model variants: plan to test two model sizes (redwood-2-xl quantized and redwood-2-large) to hit the tradeoff between latency and F1.
- Instrumentation: ensure we provide a shared tracing key and a short dashboard with per-route latency + cost. Dev, can you add the dashboard link to the eval plan?

I'll take ownership of provisioning Dedicated sandbox if we get the go-ahead from Procurement. Provision ETA ~48 hours once we have the signed commit.

Thanks — this is great. Per the asks above I've attached the short eval plan and test prompts to this thread and included the initial dashboard scope. High level:
- Eval plan: 1) baseline on hosted with redwood-2-large + redwood-2-xl quantized; 2) compare F1 on extraction test set; 3) run nightly batch throughput test (ETL) for 2 hours to measure tokens/sec.
- Dashboard: basic per-request latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), cost per token, token counts, error rate.
- Quotas: set hosted quota to 120 reqs/min and a 10k tokens/day soft cap for the first run. We can bump once we confirm stability.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting started.
